leaf_tasks.objective: Implement validated, immutable TaskId and SpecId types with stable serialization, ordering, hashing, and display.
Implement TaskClass enum for PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, REPAIR, TEST_GENERATE, ADVERSARIAL, INTEGRATE, VERIFY, RELEASE, and explicit unknown-class handling.
Implement CapabilityRequirement with capability names, quality tier, context budget, structured-output needs, and optional tool requirements.
Implement TaskContract containing ID, spec revision, class, objective, inputs, outputs, dependencies, scope, acceptance predicates, verifiers, retry policy, and risk tier.
Implement TaskState and validate every allowed state transition; reject illegal transitions.
Implement content-addressed ArtifactRef with digest, media type, size, and provenance.
Implement EvidenceReceipt linking task, attempt, artifact digests, commands, exit codes, verifier, and verdict.
Implement Verdict and FailureKind distinguishing PASS, FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE, BLOCKED, INVALID, and INFRA_ERROR.
Implement ProviderId, ModelId, EndpointId, and credential-reference types; never expose secrets in debug or serialization.
Implement shared structured errors for policy denial, quota exhaustion, timeout, transport failure, malformed output, conflicts, and verification failure.
Parse a versioned master specification into typed requirements while preserving source text and stable source locations.
Generate deterministic requirement IDs; detect duplicate IDs, collisions, and unstable source anchors.
Represent acceptance conditions as typed predicates; flag requirements lacking a testable evidence plan.
Build a traceability graph mapping every requirement to tasks, interfaces, tests, and evidence; detect uncovered requirements.
Define the planner-model input/output contract for decomposing requirements into tasks; validate every result against the source spec.
Detect oversized or mixed-responsibility tasks using configurable bounds; request decomposition rather than silently accepting them.
Reject incomplete task contracts missing objective, inputs, outputs, scope, acceptance, verifier, dependencies, or failure path.
Build a dependency DAG, detect cycles, and report a concrete cycle path.
Render deterministic one-shot worker prompts from task contracts, relevant requirements, shared contracts, and output schemas.
Emit a versioned machine-readable work-order manifest with stable IDs, dependency edges, prompt digests, and coverage statistics.
Implement a provider-independent capability catalog for coding, reviewing, repairing, test generation, adversarial analysis, and integration.
Register inference endpoints with provider, model, transport, capabilities, context window, structured-output support, and enabled status.
Validate endpoint declarations; reject invalid capabilities, impossible context settings, duplicate IDs, and missing mandatory fields.
Track endpoint health, last success, recent failures, cooldown deadline, and health confidence.
Maintain rolling latency and completion statistics by endpoint and task class.
Track evidence-based task success rates by endpoint and class; exclude unverified self-reports.
Implement deterministic capability matching between task requirements and eligible endpoints.
Estimate prompt and expected-output context usage; reject or transform work exceeding endpoint context limits.
Resolve credentials through secret references and prevent secret leakage into logs, prompts, and receipts.
Expose versioned immutable registry snapshots for reproducible scheduling decisions.
Define an async provider-neutral inference trait with typed request, response, cancellation, usage, and error structures.
Implement configurable HTTP inference transport with timeouts, response-size limits, retry classification, and redacted diagnostics.
Implement an OpenAI-compatible adapter with configurable endpoint, model, headers, structured-output mode, and usage parsing.
Implement a configurable NVIDIA inference adapter using documented endpoint settings; do not hardcode undocumented quotas.
Implement a Gemini adapter with provider-specific request/response mapping and typed quota errors.
Implement a Copilot integration boundary using supported interfaces only; return explicit unsupported status when headless automation is unavailable.
Implement a local OpenAI-compatible inference adapter with health probing and bounded requests.
Normalize provider responses into text, structured payload, usage, finish reason, request ID, and response-artifact reference.
Normalize provider errors into typed retryable/non-retryable errors while preserving safe diagnostic evidence.
Implement a reusable adapter conformance harness for timeout, malformed response, cancellation, usage accounting, and secret redaction.
Model request-rate, token-rate, daily-use, concurrency, cost, and cooldown limits independently; unknown limits remain unknown.
Implement deterministic per-endpoint token-bucket admission control with an injectable clock.
Implement an exact bounded sliding-window request-rate limiter.
Enforce endpoint-specific and global in-flight request limits.
Record provider-reported input/output tokens, requests, latency, errors, and estimated cost where available.
Model provider quota reset windows and Retry-After data without assuming universal reset behavior.
Reserve request/token/cost budgets before dispatch and reconcile or release reservations after completion or failure.
Implement configurable weighted fair allocation across task classes to prevent starvation.
Reduce dispatch rate on quota errors or rising latency and recover gradually after successful windows.
Record why each task was dispatched, delayed, rerouted, or denied due to quota, budget, or fairness policy.
Represent task graph nodes and dependency edges with stable IDs and explicit edge semantics.
Compute ready tasks whose required dependencies have passed their acceptance gates.
Implement deterministic task priority from configured risk, critical path, age, class weight, and estimated duration.
Compute critical-path depth and estimated remaining work using configurable duration estimates.
Partition ready tasks by class, required capability, context budget, and isolation needs.
Deduplicate equivalent submissions using explicit idempotency keys and spec revision; preserve tasks with different acceptance criteria.
Bound queue growth and apply deterministic backpressure.
Propagate cancellation to dependent or superseded tasks according to policy while preserving completed evidence.
Produce machine-readable reasons and dependency paths for blocked tasks.
Serialize stable queue snapshots and replay scheduling decisions from recorded inputs.
Create a dispatch envelope containing task contract, prompt digest, endpoint, limits, workspace, and expected output schema.
Dispatch eligible tasks up to available worker, endpoint, and global concurrency limits.
Enforce connection, first-token, total-response, and task deadlines with typed timeout outcomes.
Implement bounded retry policies with retry classes, backoff, injectable jitter, and retry budgets.
Support optional duplicate/hedged inference for explicitly eligible tasks when quota and policy allow it.
Validate worker output against the required schema before accepting it as a candidate artifact.
Track in-flight attempt progress without treating worker progress claims as proof.
Recover orphaned RUNNING tasks after restart using leases, attempt IDs, and durable state.
Use idempotency keys and effect receipts to prevent duplicate external side effects; explicitly document inference delivery semantics.
Expose queue wait, service time, retries, errors, utilization, and throughput by task class and endpoint.
Create isolated per-task Git worktrees or equivalent workspaces pinned to a base commit.
Compare changed paths with each task's allowed scope and reject unauthorized modifications.
Record base commit, branch, workspace ID, and spec revision for every attempt.
Capture normalized diffs and changed-file manifests as immutable artifacts before cleanup.
Hash patches and artifacts and detect post-capture mutation.
Detect overlapping changed paths and incompatible public-interface changes before integration.
Build integration workspaces from exact accepted artifact commits and record all parent revisions.
Remove abandoned worktrees only after preserving required logs, patches, receipts, and recovery metadata.
Permit local branches and commits under policy; gate pushes, protected merges, tags, releases, and destructive resets.
Record HEAD, dirty state, diff digest, submodule state, and relevant tool versions for each attempt.
Store patches, prompts, responses, logs, test output, manifests, and reports by content digest with type metadata.
Define typed events for compile, schedule, dispatch, response, verify, retry, integrate, deny, release, and failure.
Add monotonic event sequence numbers and hash chaining; document that hashing detects alteration but does not alone prevent privileged rewriting.
Persist task attempt receipts transactionally so crashes cannot record completion without evidence references.
Store the exact rendered prompt, task contract version, shared contract version, endpoint identity, and prompt digest.
Store response artifacts or bounded redacted outputs, provider request IDs, usage, finish reasons, and digests.
Link each acceptance predicate to exact evidence and the verifier version that evaluated it.
Redact credentials and configured sensitive patterns while preserving reproducibility metadata.
Query task lineage, failed gates, endpoint performance, requirement coverage, and artifact ancestry.
Export and restore verifiable ledger bundles, validating hashes, sequence continuity, schema versions, and artifact references.
Register deterministic verifier commands and typed verifier capabilities by task class and requirement predicate.
Execute configured verification commands with bounded time, output, environment, process tree, and resource limits.
Capture actual exit codes and distinguish test failure from verification-runner infrastructure failure.
Normalize supported test outputs into pass/fail/skip counts and evidence references without inventing missing results.
Evaluate each acceptance predicate independently; missing evidence yields INCONCLUSIVE or FAIL according to policy, never PASS.
Generate requirement coverage reports showing proven, failed, blocked, and unverified requirements with evidence links.
Dispatch independent review to a distinct eligible endpoint; prohibit the implementer's response from serving as its own review evidence.
Require review findings to include severity, task/requirement reference, evidence, reproduction steps, and confidence.
Cache verification results only when source digest, command, environment fingerprint, verifier version, and relevant dependencies match.
Produce verdict receipts with predicate-level outcomes, commands, versions, and evidence digests.
